findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview: started on demand (cwd = the project folder) on an OS-assigned free port that is never 8777, with its own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped when dead
findings.message: Wave 3's intent says criterion 1 is (B) and "the manager is built." The same wave's deliverable still says "Until (B) is ratified, W3.1 and its dependents spend zero." Elegance leaves W3.1 HOLD, and W4 endpoints, W5.2 lab 302, W4.2 boot reap, and W7.1 stop chip inherit that HOLD. Foreman has two sentences and they contradict. Obey the HOLD and John has no project lab, no restart of a dead one, no stop — only a classifier and some chips. Re-asking the North Star as a one-liner leaves criterion 1 unimplemented while later waves talk as if a lab exists.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> … starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The interstitial is HOLD until "a recorded click that is blank or hung under a blocking 302-after-probe." Criterion 2 already forbids that click. Wave 5's own intent admits the remaining path — a spinnerless wait on the dashboard origin — is a blank page, then the deliverable still withholds the poll. Labs are started on demand, so the first click after idle is the cold path. The rebuild trigger makes John the first failing test. A lab that is "up on first probe" skips the page; the cold start, the missing-jupyter case, and the hung pid are exactly when he clicks.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row (register, plan outline, files tile) opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file
findings.message: W6 KEEPs rewriting register, plan-step, and files rows to `/notebook` and painting "lab" / "notebook" / "editor" chips. W5.1 KEEPs the route. W5.2's dispatch to `ensure_lab` and the 302 to `/lab/tree/<rel>` stay HOLD with W3.1. John will see a clickable row that claims it opens where it runs. One implementation ships hrefs at a route with no lab branch (blank, 404, or hung tab). The other skips the rewrite because dispatch never shipped, so the same rows stay read-only artifacts. Either way a notebook row does not open in JupyterLab. The plan has no operator contract for what a click does while those HOLDs stand.

findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a http://localhost / 127.0.0.1 / <this machine's tailnet name> URL renders as a link (new window); journal 0110 — a JupyterLab or Shiny address reachable from the register and the plan without a launch page
findings.section: Wave 2 / W2.1 HOLD + Wave 8 live-link fixture
findings.message: After the probe is HOLD, `allowed_hosts` is localhost, 127.0.0.1, `socket.gethostname()` (this machine's hostname is PUTER), and whatever someone puts in `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. The 0110 address is `https://gwl-server.tailb49f65.ts.net:8446/lab`. Exact hostname equality means `gwl-server` does not match that FQDN; PUTER matches neither. Wave 2's GWT only proves `http://gwl-server/shiny/app` with the env set to the short name, and still names `fake_tailscale.py` which the HOLD forbids adding. W8 then lets sign-off use "the running managed lab's URL" instead of the tailnet row, so the ship gate can go green without the motivating host ever becoming a link. Nothing in W8 sets `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` on the live service. John clicks the register row that opened this effort and it stays text.

findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`); 5 — a long .py opens in the editor (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Criterion 3 names `code -r`. The editor page still dual-fires the seam and `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)`. vscode:// is HOLD until a recorded click where `code -r` failed, but Wave 8 (c) still captures a `vscode://file/` navigation request as the Playwright proof and defers the actual editor window to "eyes-on." Dual-fire can open the file twice. The operator proof is a dashboard tab that says "Opening … in the editor," not VS Code. If the HOLD is obeyed, the sign-off assertion on `vscode://` cannot pass. If it is not, the North Star editor path is still unshown.

findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed — never a blank page; a stale or dead lab is restarted
findings.message: `ensure_lab` treats a live pid that fails two `/api/status` probes (1.5 s each) as dead, tree-kills it, and starts fresh. Criterion 2 restarts stale or dead labs, not slow ones. A cold JupyterLab that is still binding is killed mid-boot; the next click starts another. W5 drives ensure from the route and from `lab_ready` polls, so the first-click / double-click / poll-during-boot case is the one that hits this. The GWT only uses `FAKE_LAB_HANG` (socket accepted, never answers). Restart-on-hung becomes restart-on-not-ready-yet, which is how "come up every time" becomes "never stays up."

findings.criterion: 3 — a .py or .R row that is short (≤ 120 lines) or marked as a notebook (`# %%` cells, or `# notebook` in its first lines) is converted once … and opened in JupyterLab; the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
findings.message: Criterion 3 scopes "first lines" to the `# notebook` marker only. `# %%` cells are a mark anywhere. `open_kind` only scans `# %%` inside the 121-line cap, so a 400-line percent-script whose first `# %%` sits on line 122 is `editor`, the chip says "editor", and `code -r` opens it. The GWT proves the opposite case (`# %%` on line 3 of a 400-line file). John clicking a VS Code-style notebook that starts after a long import block does not get a notebook. The row lies about where that file runs.

findings.criterion: 3 — code rows open where they run; 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet-name URL renders as a link (new window)
findings.message: The parser says a cell with both a path and a URL "keeps the path as the open target." `delivRow` takes `if (it.url)` first and never rewrites that row to `/notebook`. If `url` is still set, John clicks a `.py` and lands on the live URL. If `url` is cleared because a path exists, a register row that still has the 0110 launch-page path plus the real lab/Shiny address keeps opening the launch page — the gap this criterion exists to close. One cell cannot obey both sentences. The click is unspecified.

findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project, a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: Sign-off Given is "no lab running." Wave 5 then answers that click with a 200 interstitial on the dashboard origin whose URL is `/notebook/…`, and only later sets `window.location` to `/lab/tree/…`. Wave 8 (a) asserts the popup URL contains `/lab/tree/signoff/hello.ipynb` with no wait through `lab_ready`. On the stated cold path that assertion is false at first paint. If W5.3 HOLD also stands, there is no interstitial either — Playwright is then staring at the blank click criterion 2 forbids. Criterion 5 is not met by a screenshot of a spinnerless `/notebook` tab.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens … at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Register and plan-step rows pass `path` plus `dir=<effort-rel>`. The files tile is specified as `dir=''` and "project-relative path," and the gate only asserts that `openProducedFile` / `renderFiles` contain a `/notebook` `window.open` string. Wave 8 never clicks a files-tile row. If the files payload is effort-relative (a produced `hello.ipynb` under the campaign dir), `/notebook` joins it at the project root, the route 404s with no echo, and the third named surface is a blank tab. Criterion 2 lists that surface as equal to the register.

findings.criterion: 3 — kernel python3 or ir; Statement — short code as a Jupyter notebook in the project's own JupyterLab (Python and R kernels)
findings.message: Missing jupyter is an honest reason on the click. Missing `ir` is not. `to_notebook` still stamps `.R` with kernelspec `ir`. Wave 8 treats IRkernel as a host inventory fact and screenshots the stamp. Execution-on-open is a non-goal; shipping an R kernel in the lab is not. John clicking a short `.R` still gets a sibling notebook whose kernel the lab may not have, with no reason on the page and a "notebook" chip that says it runs.

findings.criterion: 3 — the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
findings.message: The locked words are "notebook" and "editor." The chip prints `open_kind.kind`, so a `.ipynb` row says "lab." An operator reading the row for where it runs has to know that "lab" means the notebook. Harmless if the click works; it is not the vocabulary the criterion named.

findings.criterion: 1 — a project's own JupyterLab, managed like a preview (cwd = project folder, OS-assigned port never 8777, own token, registered, listed, stoppable, reaped)
findings.section: Wave 3 intent vs W3.1 HOLD / elegance pass
findings.message: The locked criterion is the per-project lab. Wave 3’s own Intent says that locked line “IS option (B) … so the manager is built.” The elegance table then HOLDs W3.1 and every dependent (ensure/probe/reap, fake_lab, labs endpoints, boot reap, healthcheck walk, `rnd labs`, Lab chip) until John picks (A) jupyter-serve or (B) a new lab, and orders “spend zero” until (B). Those two sentences cannot both be the build contract. (A) is not criterion 1: not per-project, not cwd = the project folder, not an OS-assigned port, not registered/listed/stoppable/reaped like a preview. A Foreman that honors HOLDs ships no lab. A Foreman that honors wave text builds a manager the table forbids. Criterion 1 is not a measurement you can take until the independent variable (which process is “the project’s own JupyterLab”) is fixed to one treatment.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file (starting the lab if needed)
findings.message: Kind-dispatch is KEEP’d; the Location it 302s to is HOLD’d. If HOLDs win, `/notebook` exists and has nowhere to send the browser. If (B) is built, the click goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/…` of a lab W3.1 is not allowed to spawn. If (A) is wired instead, `/lab/tree/<rel>` is relative to jupyter-serve’s root, not the project folder, so an in-effort notebook is a 404 or the wrong tree — and nothing starts or restarts a dead lab. Criterion 2 is one click that lands on that file in that project’s lab. This route, as HOLD’d, has no such target. W5.1 KEEP of the path is not a substitute for a destination.

findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.section: Wave 5 — dispatch vs W5.3 HOLD (interstitial / lab_ready)
findings.message: The same wave requires `'lab' -> lab_server.ensure_lab -> 302` and, in the next sentence, that a cold lab “answers immediately” via a poll page whose start is backgrounded. W3.2’s `ensure_lab` still waits `health_timeout=20`. Those are two control flows; the plan does not name which thread starts the process. W5.3 then HOLDs both the interstitial and `lab_ready` until a recorded click is blank or hung under a blocking 302. Criterion 2 forbids that blank page; using the forbidden outcome as the trigger to build the mitigation is how the failure ships. What remains is 302-after-probe. A cold JupyterLab boot is then a silent tab — connection-refused or a spinnerless wait — which the wave’s own Intent already admits is a blank page. `fake_lab` answers at once, so W3–W7 never see a real boot; W8 is the first clocked start, after the mechanism is parked.

findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected, a short .py opens as a notebook, a long .py opens in the editor, a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: The six screenshots do not measure the four locked claims. (a) “file selected” is a document title containing the basename; `fake_lab` is specified to serve exactly `<title><basename></title>` for `/lab/tree/<rel>`, so the stub teaches the gate a tautology, and a real JupyterLab shell with the path only in the URL can pass. (c) is “eyes-on” that VS Code has the file, while the automated assert is a `vscode://file/` href — not `code -r`. (d) allows the fixture URL to be the pre-existing tailnet jupyter-serve at `:8446` “or” the managed lab; a green `04-live-link.png` then does not corroborate that a project lab came up. That is a confound: the live-link treatment can be the old server while criteria 1–2 still fail. Criterion 5 is eyes on the opens on the surface he uses, not URL-shape lints plus a PNG of an interstitial.

findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`), and the row says which
findings.message: The locked launcher is `code -r <file>`. The editor page still dual-fires `ANCHOR_EDITOR_CMD` and `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)`, which can open the file twice and put an absolute path in page history. W5.4 HOLDs the URI half “until a recorded click where `code -r` did not land,” while W5’s deliverable and W8’s pass condition still require a `vscode://file/` href and capture that navigation. The live gate is wired to the parked half. Remote `vscode://` on a tablet is the parked non-goal (iPad editing). Criterion 3 is satisfied by a non-blocking `code -r` that actually raises the file. Prove that seam; do not gate on the scheme the HOLD forbids.

findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, or this machine's tailnet name renders as a link; every other host stays text
findings.section: Wave 2 — W2.1 HOLD / Wave 2 GWT / Wave 8 live-link fixture
findings.message: Production resolution of “this machine’s tailnet name” after the W2.1 HOLD is `localhost` + `127.0.0.1` + `socket.gethostname()` (this host’s friendly name is not guaranteed to be the tailnet name) plus an optional `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. The auto-probe that would have read `Self.DNSName` is parked; `tests/fake_tailscale.py` is not earned. The wave’s own Given/When/Then still requires `ANCHOR_TAILSCALE_CMD` pointing at that stub and the stub’s DNSName to return a URL — an acceptance test of a HOLD’d path. Sign-off injects `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` and then confirms the override, which is not evidence the NSSM `anchor` service knows the FQDN on a boot where the env is unset. Journal 0110’s URL is that FQDN. Criterion 4 is a row John can click without a test-only env, not a stubbed frozenset.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens at /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Files-tile clicks are `window.open` of `/notebook` with `dir=''` on the claim that “the path is project-relative there.” The plan does not show that the files payload actually carries project-root-relative paths. The register already has `dir` because effort-relative paths are a real case. If a produced file is effort-relative, `dir=''` joins to a path that fails containment or 404s, and the files tile is the one named surface that never starts the lab on the right file. No Given/When/Then uses a files-tile row; the JS is asserted textually. Criterion 2 names that tile. Register and plan inherit `dir`; files are specified as if they do not need it, without a proof that the producer agrees.

findings.criterion: 3 — the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
findings.message: The locked labels are notebook and editor. The chip also prints `lab` for `.ipynb`. That is a third word the criterion does not use, so a notebook row does not “say which” in the vocabulary the surface locked. Harmless if renamed; as specified it fails the letter of criterion 3 on the most common row.

findings.criterion: 5 — seen on the page before it ships … Playwright screenshots, then the release pipeline
findings.section: plan header test-command vs Wave 8 gate
findings.message: The machine-countable `test-command` is three files (`test_code_windows_2026_09_07.py`, `test_steward_deliverables.py`, `test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`). Criterion 5 is the page, then the pipeline; a gate that cannot see the sign-off is not that criterion. Name one command that actually counts the surfaces you claim, or admit the header command is a lint.

Those two sentences cannot both be the build contract. (A) is not criterion 1: not per-project, not cwd = the project folder, not an OS-assigned port, not registered/listed/stoppable/reaped like a preview. A Foreman that honors HOLDs ships no lab. A Foreman that honors wave text builds a manager the table forbids. Criterion 1 is not a measurement you can take until the independent variable (which process is “the project’s own JupyterLab”) is fixed to one treatment.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb row opens in a new window at the lab's /lab/tree/<rel> for that file (starting the lab if needed)
findings.message: Kind-dispatch is KEEP’d; the Location it 302s to is HOLD’d. If HOLDs win, `/notebook` exists and has nowhere to send the browser. If (B) is built, the click goes to `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/lab/tree/…` of a lab W3.1 is not allowed to spawn. If (A) is wired instead, `/lab/tree/<rel>` is relative to jupyter-serve’s root, not the project folder, so an in-effort notebook is a 404 or the wrong tree — and nothing starts or restarts a dead lab. Criterion 2 is one click that lands on that file in that project’s lab. This route, as HOLD’d, has no such target. W5.1 KEEP of the path is not a substitute for a destination.

findings.section: Wave 5 — dispatch vs W5.3 HOLD (interstitial / lab_ready)
findings.criterion: 2 — starting or restarting the lab if needed; a stale or dead lab is restarted, never a blank page
findings.message: The same wave requires `'lab' -> lab_server.ensure_lab -> 302` and, in the next sentence, that a cold lab “answers immediately” via a poll page whose start is backgrounded. W3.2’s `ensure_lab` still waits `health_timeout=20`. Those are two control flows; the plan does not name which thread starts the process. W5.3 then HOLDs both the interstitial and `lab_ready` until a recorded click is blank or hung under a blocking 302. Criterion 2 forbids that blank page; using the forbidden outcome as the trigger to build the mitigation is how the failure ships. What remains is 302-after-probe. A cold JupyterLab boot is then a silent tab — connection-refused or a spinnerless wait — which the wave’s own Intent already admits is a blank page. `fake_lab` answers at once, so W3–W7 never see a real boot; W8 is the first clocked start, after the mechanism is parked.

findings.topic: sign-off does not observe the opens
findings.criterion: 5 — on a real project a .ipynb row opens the lab with the file selected, a short .py opens as a notebook, a long .py opens in the editor, a live-link row opens (Playwright screenshots)
findings.message: The six screenshots do not measure the four locked claims. (a) “file selected” is a document title containing the basename; `fake_lab` is specified to serve exactly `<title><basename></title>` for `/lab/tree/<rel>`, so the stub teaches the gate a tautology, and a real JupyterLab shell with the path only in the URL can pass. (c) is “eyes-on” that VS Code has the file, while the automated assert is a `vscode://file/` href — not `code -r`. (d) allows the fixture URL to be the pre-existing tailnet jupyter-serve at `:8446` “or” the managed lab; a green `04-live-link.png` then does not corroborate that a project lab came up. That is a confound: the live-link treatment can be the old server while criteria 1–2 still fail. Criterion 5 is eyes on the opens on the surface he uses, not URL-shape lints plus a PNG of an interstitial.

findings.criterion: 3 — longer code opens in the editor (VS Code on this machine, `code -r <file>`), and the row says which
findings.message: The locked launcher is `code -r <file>`. The editor page still dual-fires `ANCHOR_EDITOR_CMD` and `location.assign(vscode://file/<abs>)`, which can open the file twice and put an absolute path in page history. W5.4 HOLDs the URI half “until a recorded click where `code -r` did not land,” while W5’s deliverable and W8’s pass condition still require a `vscode://file/` href and capture that navigation. The live gate is wired to the parked half. Remote `vscode://` on a tablet is the parked non-goal (iPad editing). Criterion 3 is satisfied by a non-blocking `code -r` that actually raises the file. Prove that seam; do not gate on the scheme the HOLD forbids.

findings.section: Wave 2 — W2.1 HOLD / Wave 2 GWT / Wave 8 live-link fixture
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is http://localhost, 127.0.0.1, or this machine's tailnet name renders as a link; every other host stays text
findings.message: Production resolution of “this machine’s tailnet name” after the W2.1 HOLD is `localhost` + `127.0.0.1` + `socket.gethostname()` (this host’s friendly name is not guaranteed to be the tailnet name) plus an optional `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES`. The auto-probe that would have read `Self.DNSName` is parked; `tests/fake_tailscale.py` is not earned. The wave’s own Given/When/Then still requires `ANCHOR_TAILSCALE_CMD` pointing at that stub and the stub’s DNSName to return a URL — an acceptance test of a HOLD’d path. Sign-off injects `ANCHOR_TAILNET_NAMES` and then confirms the override, which is not evidence the NSSM `anchor` service knows the FQDN on a boot where the env is unset. Journal 0110’s URL is that FQDN. Criterion 4 is a row John can click without a test-only env, not a stubbed frozenset.

findings.criterion: 2 — a .ipynb in the register, under its step in the plan, or in the files tile opens at /lab/tree/<rel>
findings.message: Files-tile clicks are `window.open` of `/notebook` with `dir=''` on the claim that “the path is project-relative there.” The plan does not show that the files payload actually carries project-root-relative paths. The register already has `dir` because effort-relative paths are a real case. If a produced file is effort-relative, `dir=''` joins to a path that fails containment or 404s, and the files tile is the one named surface that never starts the lab on the right file. No Given/When/Then uses a files-tile row; the JS is asserted textually. Criterion 2 names that tile. Register and plan inherit `dir`; files are specified as if they do not need it, without a proof that the producer agrees.

findings.topic: mixed Where cell url vs path
findings.criterion: 4 — a Where cell that is a localhost / 127.0.0.1 / tailnet URL renders as a link (new window)
findings.message: The parser says a cell carrying both a path and a URL “keeps the path as the open target.” The renderer’s first branch is `if (it.url)` → `<a href=it.url>`. Those cannot both be true of the same row. If `url` is set, the live link wins and the path is dead. If `url` is withheld whenever a path is present, the journal-0110 workaround rows (`RUN-*.html` launch pages whose Where cell also mentions the tailnet address) stay path-opens and criterion 4 does not fire on the rows that motivated it. The plan never says which encoding existing registers use, and never migrates them. A construct that is specified two ways is untestable: W6’s fixture rows are pure URL or pure path, so the mixed case — the actual 0110 shape — is never observed.

findings.criterion: 3 — the row says which ("notebook" / "editor")
findings.message: The locked labels are notebook and editor. The chip also prints `lab` for `.ipynb`. That is a third word the criterion does not use, so a notebook row does not “say which” in the vocabulary the surface locked. Harmless if renamed; as specified it fails the letter of criterion 3 on the most common row.

findings.section: plan header test-command vs Wave 8 gate
findings.criterion: 5 — seen on the page before it ships … Playwright screenshots, then the release pipeline
findings.message: The machine-countable `test-command` is three files (`test_code_windows_2026_09_07.py`, `test_steward_deliverables.py`, `test_reports_links_2026_09_05.py`). W8’s “nets green” bar is the full suite plus per-wave stub gates plus Playwright sign-off. If Foreman runs the header command, W0/W1b/W2/W3/W4 stub files and `test_code_opens_signoff_w4.py` never have to pass. Criterion 5 is the page, then the pipeline; a gate that cannot see the sign-off is not that criterion. Name one command that actually counts the surfaces you claim, or admit the header command is a lint.
